items.title: Mean-zero Poincare inequality on the normalized torus
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $N\ge1$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized Lebesgue measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For a smooth real vector field $f:Q_d\to\mathbb R^N$, define its mean by $\bar f=\int_{Q_d}f\,d\mu$ and the Frobenius gradient norm by $|\nabla f|^2=\sum_{a=1}^N\sum_{j=1}^d|\partial_j f_a|^2$. If $\bar f=0$, then $\|f\|_{L^2(Q_d)}\le\|\nabla f\|_{L^2(Q_d)}$.

references.title: Sergei Kuksin and Armen Shirikyan, Mathematics of Two-Dimensional Turbulence, §2.1.7

items.title: Smooth Sobolev continuation criterion
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For the periodic incompressible IVP with $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\nu\ge0$, smooth real divergence-free initial data on the normalized torus $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, and integer $s\ge4$, let $u$ be the unique maximal smooth solution on $[0,T^*)$. Maximal means that no smooth solution in the same class on a larger interval agrees with $u$ on $[0,T^*)$. If $T^*<\infty$ and $\sup_{t<T^*}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}<\infty$, then $u$ extends smoothly to an interval $[0,T^*+\epsilon]$ for some $\epsilon>0$.

For the positive-density polytropic Euler IVP with $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\kappa>0$, $\gamma>1$, and integer $s\ge4$, let $q=(r,u)$ be the unique maximal smooth solution in the symmetric variables from the stated definition, on $[0,T^*)$, with $r(t,x)>0$. If $T^*<\infty$, $\sup_{t<T^*}\|q(t)\|_{H^s}<\infty$, and $\inf_{t<T^*,\,x\in Q_d}r(t,x)>0$, then $q$ and its positive density $\rho=(ar/\sqrt{\kappa\gamma})^{1/a}$ extend smoothly beyond $T^*$.

references.title: Sergei Kuksin and Armen Shirikyan, Mathematics of Two-Dimensional Turbulence, Chapter 2, §§2.1.5–2.1.6
David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2

items.title: Smooth polytropic energy conservation
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\kappa>0$, $\gamma>1$, $a=(\gamma-1)/2$, integer $s\ge4$, and smooth real periodic data $\rho_0:Q_d\to(0,\infty)$ and $u_0:Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$ on the normalized torus $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, with $\min_{x\in Q_d}\rho_0(x)>0$. Use normalized Lebesgue measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, Fourier coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int_{Q_d}f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, and norms $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+|k|^2)^m|\widehat f(k)|^2$. For $\rho>0$, set $r(\rho)=\sqrt{\kappa\gamma}\rho^a/a$. The local positive-density polytropic Euler theorem supplies a unique smooth solution $(\rho,u)$ on $[0,T]$ with these initial data and $\rho(t,x)>0$, where $T$ depends only on $d,s,\kappa,\gamma,\|(r(\rho_0),u_0)\|_{H^s}$ and $\min_{x\in Q_d}r(\rho_0)(x)$, satisfying
$$\rho_t+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad u_t+u\cdot\nabla u+\rho^{-1}\nabla p(\rho)=0,\qquad p(\rho)=\kappa\rho^\gamma.$$
Define the internal-energy density $U(\rho)=\kappa\rho^\gamma/(\gamma-1)$ and total-energy density $E=\frac12\rho|u|^2+U(\rho)$. Then
$$\partial_tE+\operatorname{div}((E+p(\rho))u)=0,$$
and the total energy $\int_{Q_d}E(t,x)\,d\mu(x)$ is constant on $[0,T]$.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3, §4.5
François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, Chapter 3

items.title: Conditional wall energy and smooth uniqueness
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set with $C^2$ boundary, meaning that after a rigid coordinate change each boundary patch is the graph $z=h(y)$ of a $C^2$ function and $\Omega$ lies locally on one side. Let $n$ be the outward unit normal and let $dS$ be the chart-independent Euclidean surface measure. Fix constant density $\rho>0$, constant viscosity $\eta>0$, slip coefficient $\beta\ge0$, and a continuous force field $b:[0,T]\times\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$. Suppose $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C([0,T];C^1(\overline\Omega))$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \rho(u_t+u\cdot\nabla u)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b,\qquad \sigma=-pI+2\eta D,\qquad D=\frac{\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}}2.$$
For a vector $a$, write $a_{\tan}=a-(a\cdot n)n$. Under either stationary no-slip data $u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ or impermeable Navier-slip data $u\cdot n=0$ and $(\sigma n)_{\tan}=-\beta u_{\tan}$, define $K(t)=\frac12\rho\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2\,dx$. In the no-slip case,
$$K'(t)=\rho\int_\Omega b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega|D|^2\,dx;$$
in the slip case,
$$K'(t)=\rho\int_\Omega b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega|D|^2\,dx-\beta\int_{\partial\Omega}|u_{\tan}|^2\,dS.$$
If two smooth velocity solutions satisfy the same equation, force, initial velocity, density, viscosity, and selected wall law, then their velocities are equal on $[0,T]$. This is conditional on the given smooth solutions and asserts no wall-flow existence theorem.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2, §§3.1.1–3.1.2

items.title: Fluid equation scalings and dimensionless numbers
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\ell>0$, and $\nu\ge0$, and write $Q_\ell=\mathbb R^d/(\ell\mathbb Z)^d$. For a period cell, define $\|f\|_{L^2_{\rm vol}(Q_\ell)}=(\int_{[0,\ell]^d}|f(x)|^2dx)^{1/2}$. First, if a smooth velocity-pressure pair on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$ or $[0,T]\times Q_\ell$ solves the unforced incompressible Navier–Stokes system
$$u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla\pi+\nu\Delta u,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0,$$
then for any $\lambda>0$,
$$u_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda u(\lambda^2t,\lambda x),\qquad \pi_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda^2\pi(\lambda^2t,\lambda x)$$
solves the same system with the same viscosity on $\mathbb R^d$ or on the torus of period $\ell/\lambda$, respectively, for $0\le t\le T/\lambda^2$. On the torus, use the Fourier Leray multiplier $P_0=I$, $P_\xi=I-\xi\xi^{\mathsf T}/|\xi|^2$ for $\xi\ne0$; the projected equation is preserved as well because $P_{\lambda\xi}=P_\xi$. For a cell-volume $L^2$ norm, $\|u_\lambda(0)\|_{L^2_{\rm vol}(Q_{\ell/\lambda})}=\lambda^{1-d/2}\|u(0)\|_{L^2_{\rm vol}(Q_\ell)}$.

Second, for any $\alpha,\beta>0$, if $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is open and a smooth pair $(u,\pi)$ on $[0,T]\times\Omega$ solves the unforced incompressible Euler system $u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla\pi$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, then on the scaled domain $\beta^{-1}\Omega$,
$$u_{\alpha,\beta}(t,x)=\alpha u(\alpha\beta t,\beta x),\qquad \pi_{\alpha,\beta}(t,x)=\alpha^2\pi(\alpha\beta t,\beta x)$$
solves the same equation on the correspondingly scaled domain and time interval $0\le t\le T/(\alpha\beta)$. These transformations are equation symmetries; on a torus they transform its period.

Finally, let $U,L,\rho_*,\eta>0$ be physical scales in SI units, with $U$ and sound speed in m/s, $L$ in m, $\rho_*$ in kg/m$^3$, dynamic viscosity $\eta$ in Pa$\cdot$s, kinematic viscosity $\nu=\eta/\rho_*$ in m$^2$/s, and kinematic pressure $\pi_{\rm phys}$ in m$^2$/s$^2$. The substitution $X=Lx$, $t_{\rm phys}=(L/U)t$, $u_{\rm phys}=Uu$, and $\pi_{\rm phys}=U^2\pi$ gives the dimensionless incompressible Navier–Stokes coefficient $Re^{-1}$, where $Re=UL/\nu=\rho_*UL/\eta$. Let $p$ be differentiable at the positive reference density $\rho_*$, with pressure measured in Pa and $p'(\rho_*)>0$ in m$^2$/s$^2$, and sound speed $c_*=\sqrt{p'(\rho_*)}$. For the linear acoustic tangent system $\delta\rho_t+\rho_*\operatorname{div}v_{\rm phys}=0$, $(v_{\rm phys})_t+(c_*^2/\rho_*)\nabla_X\delta\rho=0$, where $\delta\rho$ has units kg/m$^3$, the scales $X=Lx$, $t_{\rm phys}=(L/U)t$, $\delta\rho=\rho_*\delta\rho'$, and $v_{\rm phys}=Uv$ give the momentum coefficient $Ma^{-2}$, where $Ma=U/c_*$. Both $Re$ and $Ma$ are dimensionless. These are chain-rule identities and assert no continuum limit or empirical similarity.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2, §3.3.1
David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3, §4.4.4

items.title: Two-dimensional Fourier logarithmic velocity bound
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $Q_2=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ have normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-2}dx$, Fourier coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int_{Q_2}f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, weights $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and Sobolev norms $\|f\|_{H^r}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^2}w_k^{2r}|\widehat f(k)|^2$, componentwise for vector fields. For an integer $m\ge4$ and smooth real divergence-free $u:Q_2\to\mathbb R^2$, define $\omega=\partial_1u_2-\partial_2u_1$, $Y=\|u\|_{H^m}$, $B=\|\omega\|_{H^1}$, and $S=\sum_{k\ne0}|k|\,|\widehat u(k)|$. Then $S<\infty$ and there is a constant $C_m$ depending only on $m$ such that
$$S\le C_m\left(1+B\sqrt{\log(e+Y)}\right).$$

references.title: Sergei Kuksin and Armen Shirikyan, Mathematics of Two-Dimensional Turbulence, Chapter 2, §2.1.6, Theorem 2.1.18
references.locator: PDF pp. 45–51; the local proof here instead establishes the stated Fourier lattice estimate directly.

items.title: A longitudinal acoustic Fourier mode conserves weighted energy
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; exact argument, source scope and dependencies are recorded in batch-19 notes.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\rho_*>0$, and $c_*>0$. On the torus $Q_2=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ with normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-2}dx$, let $e_1,e_2$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb R^2$ and choose $A,B,W\in\mathbb R$. Put
$$Z(t)=A\cos(c_*t)-\frac{\rho_*B}{c_*}\sin(c_*t),\qquad V(t)=B\cos(c_*t)+\frac{c_*A}{\rho_*}\sin(c_*t),$$
$$z(t,x)=Z(t)\cos x_1,\qquad v(t,x)=V(t)\sin x_1\,e_1+W e_2.$$
Then $(z,v)$ solves the linear acoustic tangent system $z_t+\rho_*\operatorname{div}v=0$, $v_t+(c_*^2/\rho_*)\nabla z=0$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, with initial data $z(0,x)=A\cos x_1$ and $v(0,x)=B\sin x_1e_1+We_2$. Its weighted energy is constant and equals
$$\|v(t)\|_{L^2(Q_2)}^2+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*^2}\|z(t)\|_{L^2(Q_2)}^2=W^2+\frac12\left(B^2+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*^2}A^2\right).$$

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3, §4.4.4
references.locator: PDF pp. 150–153; the example is an exact mode of the linear tangent system, with its normalized-torus calculation given here.
